claim: Natural selection of variants within the Arabidopsis thaliana circadian clock can be attributed to adaptation to varying environments.
source: Natural selection of variants within the Arabidopsis thaliana circadian clock can be attributed to adaptation to varying environments.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general principle motivating the study.

claim: Extensive variation in clock speed in a reporter-modified Bay-0 x Shakdara recombinant inbred line led to identification of EARLY FLOWERING3 (ELF3) as a major quantitative trait locus (QTL).
source: Extensive variation led us to identify EARLY FLOWERING3 (ELF3) as a major quantitative trait locus (QTL).
evidence: The abstract states that examination of clock speed variation led to identification of ELF3 as a major QTL.

claim: The causal nucleotide polymorphism in ELF3-Sha caused a short-period phenotype under light.
source: The causal nucleotide polymorphism caused a short-period phenotype under light and severely dampened rhythm generation in darkness, and entrainment alterations resulted.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this phenotype was caused by the nucleotide polymorphism.

claim: The causal nucleotide polymorphism in ELF3-Sha severely dampened rhythm generation in darkness.
source: The causal nucleotide polymorphism caused a short-period phenotype under light and severely dampened rhythm generation in darkness, and entrainment alterations resulted.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this phenotype was caused by the nucleotide polymorphism.

claim: The causal nucleotide polymorphism in ELF3-Sha resulted in entrainment alterations.
source: The causal nucleotide polymorphism caused a short-period phenotype under light and severely dampened rhythm generation in darkness, and entrainment alterations resulted.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states entrainment alterations resulted from the polymorphism.

claim: ELF3-Sha protein failed to properly localize to the nucleus.
source: We found that ELF3-Sha protein failed to properly localize to the nucleus, and its ability to accumulate in darkness was compromised.
evidence: The abstract states this finding directly.

claim: ELF3-Sha protein's ability to accumulate in darkness was compromised.
source: We found that ELF3-Sha protein failed to properly localize to the nucleus, and its ability to accumulate in darkness was compromised.
evidence: The abstract states this finding directly.

claim: The ELF3-Sha allele originated in Central Asia.
source: Evidence was provided that the ELF3-Sha allele originated in Central Asia.
evidence: The abstract states evidence was provided for this origin.

claim: ELF3 protein plays a vital role in defining its light-repressor action in the circadian clock.
source: Collectively, we showed that ELF3 protein plays a vital role in defining its light-repressor action in the circadian clock and that its functional abilities are largely dependent on its cellular localization.
evidence: The abstract concludes with this statement based on the study findings.

claim: ELF3 protein's functional abilities are largely dependent on its cellular localization.
source: Collectively, we showed that ELF3 protein plays a vital role in defining its light-repressor action in the circadian clock and that its functional abilities are largely dependent on its cellular localization.
evidence: The abstract concludes with this statement based on the study findings.

claim: The rotation of the earth leads to environmental changes in ambient light and temperature that define a 24-hr cycle.
source: The rotation of the earth leads to environmental changes in ambient light and temperature that define a 24-hr cycle.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: During diurnal cycles, light is correlated with warmth, while darkness is correlated with coolness.
source: During these diurnal cycles, light is correlated with warmth, while darkness is correlated with coolness.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Many organisms have evolved an internal timing mechanism to predict cyclic environmental cues, termed the circadian clock.
source: Thus, to ensure fitness in response to such regular environmental oscillations, many organisms have evolved an internal timing mechanism to predict these cyclic environmental cues, and this is termed the circadian clock.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The circadian clock synchronizes major developmental and physiological processes.
source: This internal clock synchronizes major developmental and physiological processes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: A considerable proportion of metabolism is under clock control.
source: For example, a considerable proportion of metabolism is under clock control (Graf et al., 2010; Haydon et al., 2011; Sanchez et al., 2011; Sanchez-Villarreal et al., 2013), and seasonal developmental programs require a circadian oscillator (Thines and Harmon, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Seasonal developmental programs require a circadian oscillator.
source: For example, a considerable proportion of metabolism is under clock control (Graf et al., 2010; Haydon et al., 2011; Sanchez et al., 2011; Sanchez-Villarreal et al., 2013), and seasonal developmental programs require a circadian oscillator (Thines and Harmon, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Thines and Harmon, 2011.

claim: The coordination of molecular and physiological processes with the external environment provides an adaptive advantage under diverse climatic conditions.
source: The coordination of molecular and physiological processes with the external environment thus provides an adaptive advantage under diverse climatic conditions (Dodd et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Dodd et al., 2005.

claim: Circadian rhythms are produced by molecular oscillators comprised of interlocking feedback loops having several components.
source: Circadian rhythms are produced by molecular oscillators, which are comprised of interlocking feedback loops having several components (Bujdoso and Davis, 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: In Arabidopsis, the central loop consists of CCA1, LHY, and TOC1.
source: In Arabidopsis, the central loop consists of two closely related single-myb transcription factors, CIRCADIAN CLOCK ASSOCIATED 1 (CCA1) and LATE ELONGATED HYPOCOTYL (LHY), as well as the pseudo response regulator (PRR) TIMING OF CAB EXPRESSION 1 (TOC1).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the Arabidopsis clock.

claim: In the morning, CCA1 and LHY repress TOC1 by directly binding to its promoter.
source: In the morning, CCA1 and LHY repress TOC1 by directly binding to its promoter, resulting in the evening accumulation of TOC1, which, in turn, represses CCA1 and LHY expression (Gendron et al., 2012; Huang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gendron et al., 2012 and Huang et al., 2012.

claim: TOC1 accumulates in the evening and represses CCA1 and LHY expression.
source: In the morning, CCA1 and LHY repress TOC1 by directly binding to its promoter, resulting in the evening accumulation of TOC1, which, in turn, represses CCA1 and LHY expression (Gendron et al., 2012; Huang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gendron et al., 2012 and Huang et al., 2012.

claim: The evening loop is proposed to include GIGANTEA (GI) and TOC1, where GI activates the expression of TOC1, and TOC1 represses GI.
source: The evening loop is proposed to include GIGANTEA (GI) and TOC1, where GI activates the expression of TOC1, and TOC1 represses GI (Locke et al., 2006; Zeilinger et al., 2006; Huang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Locke et al., 2006, Zeilinger et al., 2006, and Huang et al., 2012.

claim: PRR7 and PRR9 repress CCA1 and LHY during the day, establishing the morning loop.
source: Two members of the pseudo response regulator gene family, PRR7 and PRR9, repress CCA1 and LHY during the day, and this establishes the morning loop (Locke et al., 2006; Zeilinger et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Locke et al., 2006 and Zeilinger et al., 2006.

claim: An evening complex comprising ELF3, ELF4, and LUX represses the morning loop by specifically binding to the PRR9 promoter to mediate transcription repression.
source: Recently, an evening complex comprising EARLY FLOWERING 3 (ELF3), EARLY FLOWERING 4 (ELF4), and LUX ARRYTHMO (LUX) has been found to repress the morning loop by specifically binding to the PRR9 promoter to mediate transcription repression (Nozue et al., 2007; Kolmos et al., 2009; Dixon et al., 2011; Helfer et al., 2011; Nusinow et al., 2011; Chow et al., 2012; Herrero and Davis, 2012; Herrero et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to recent work.

claim: Ambient light and temperature are two important environmental factors (zeitgebers) which reset the clock in a process referred to as entrainment.
source: Ambient light and temperature are two important environmental factors, termed zeitgebers, which reset the clock in a process referred to as entrainment (McClung and Davis, 2010; McClung, 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: PRR7 and PRR9 have been reported to play a role in temperature compensation.
source: PRR7 and PRR9 have been reported to play a role in temperature compensation, which is the resistance of period change under differing mean ambient temperatures (Salomé and McClung, 2005; Salome et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Salomé and McClung, 2005 and Salome et al., 2010.

claim: Continuous irradiation shortens free-running period length in a fluence-rate-dependent manner as a process termed parametric entrainment.
source: In contrast, light has been established as a key factor for the entrainment of the clock where continuous irradiation shortens free-running period length in a fluence-rate-dependent manner as a process termed parametric entrainment (Aschoff, 1979; Covington et al., 2001; Johnson et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Aschoff, 1979, Covington et al., 2001, and Johnson et al., 2003.

claim: Many observable rhythms in plants dampen in constant darkness (DD).
source: Several studies have shown that many observable rhythms in plants dampen in constant darkness (DD), where dampening is defined as a reduction in circadian amplitude.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from several studies.

claim: Many genes associated with circadian rhythms of mRNA abundance are expressed robustly under constant light (LL), but dampen in DD.
source: For example, many genes have been associated with circadian rhythms of mRNA abundance that are expressed robustly under constant light (LL), but dampen in DD (Watillon et al., 1993; Zhong et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Watillon et al., 1993 and Zhong et al., 1997.

claim: The cyclic protein accumulation of GI and ELF3 was found to be reduced when shifted to darkness.
source: Furthermore, the cyclic protein accumulation of several clock-regulated components, such as GI and ELF3 (Liu et al., 2001; David et al., 2006), was found to be reduced when shifted to darkness.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Liu et al., 2001 and David et al., 2006.

claim: Molecular and genetic studies support the involvement of ELF3 in light gating to the circadian clock.
source: Molecular and genetic studies support the involvement of ELF3 in light gating to the circadian clock, and ELF3 is also a required component of the core oscillator (Covington et al., 2001; Thines and Harmon, 2010; Kolmos et al., 2011; Herrero et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: ELF3 is a required component of the core oscillator.
source: Molecular and genetic studies support the involvement of ELF3 in light gating to the circadian clock, and ELF3 is also a required component of the core oscillator (Covington et al., 2001; Thines and Harmon, 2010; Kolmos et al., 2011; Herrero et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The elf3 mutant was originally isolated in a screen for lines displaying photoperiod-independent early flowering.
source: The elf3 mutant was originally isolated in a screen for lines displaying photoperiod-independent early flowering (Zagotta et al., 1992, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Zagotta et al., 1992, 1996.

claim: elf3 mutants display defects in clock-regulated leaf movement rhythms, rhythmic hypocotyl elongation, and arrhythmic expression of gene expression under free running conditions.
source: Further characterization of elf3 revealed other severe phenotypes, including defects in clock-regulated leaf movement rhythms, rhythmic hypocotyl elongation, and arrhythmic expression of gene expression under the free running condition of LL and in DD (Hicks et al., 1996; Reed et al., 2000; Thines and Harmon, 2010; Kolmos et al., 2011; Herrero et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Natural variation at ELF3 has been detected that could be associated to an alteration in shade-avoidance responses.
source: Natural variation at ELF3 has been detected that could be associated to an alteration in shade-avoidance responses, which included increased elongation of the hypocotyl, delay of cotyledon opening in seedlings, increased elongation of stems and petioles, and reduced developmental timing in adults, and to changes in circadian function (Tajima et al., 2007; Jimenez-Gomez et al., 2010; Coluccio et al., 2011; Undurraga et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: ELF3 was cloned and reported to encode a nuclear protein of unknown function.
source: ELF3 was cloned and reported to encode a nuclear protein of unknown function, and it was proposed to work as a transcription factor (Hicks et al., 2001; Liu et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hicks et al., 2001 and Liu et al., 2001.

claim: ELF3 protein abundance is dependent on ambient light, accumulating upon shifting plants to LL and decreasing when plants were shifted to DD.
source: Based on the accumulation of ELF3 protein upon shifting plants to LL, and its decrease when plants were shifted to DD, it was concluded that its abundance is dependent on ambient light (Liu et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Liu et al., 2001.

claim: ELF3 fulfills the zeitnehmer concept, acting to bridge light perception to the clock.
source: To extend this hypothesis based on the reported light-dependent phenotypes of elf3, McWatters et al. (2000) proposed that ELF3 fulfills the so-called zeitnehmer concept, in that this factor acts to bridge light perception to the clock.
evidence: This is a proposal from McWatters et al. (2000).

claim: ELF3 physically interacts with the phytochromeB photoreceptor.
source: This idea was further strengthened when ELF3 was found to physically interact with the phytochromeB photoreceptor (Liu et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Liu et al., 2001.

claim: The role of ELF3 in light input to the circadian clock is not altered by new findings that ELF3 is core to the oscillator.
source: The previously noted role of ELF3 in light input to the circadian clock (Kolmos et al., 2011) is not altered by new findings that ELF3 is core to the oscillator.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of recent findings with citation.

claim: The species distribution of Arabidopsis ranges from the equator to extreme northern latitudes near the Arctic Circle.
source: Worldwide, the species distribution of Arabidopsis ranges from the equator to extreme northern latitudes near the Arctic Circle (Koornneef et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Koornneef et al., 2004.

claim: Environmental variations across and within local populations of Arabidopsis act as a discriminatory force on the gene pool from which only a few genetic variants of adaptive phenotypes will be selected.
source: More specifically, environmental variations across and within local populations of Arabidopsis act as a discriminatory force on the gene pool from which only a few genetic variants of adaptive phenotypes will be selected and pass through reproduction.
evidence: This is stated as a principle of natural selection.

claim: QTL mapping was used to explain circadian parameters associated with natural variation in the circadian rhythmicity of leaf movement.
source: For example, quantitative trait locus (QTL) mapping was used to explain circadian parameters associated with natural variation in the circadian rhythmicity of leaf movement (Swarup et al., 1999; Michael et al., 2003; Edwards et al., 2005; Anwer and Davis, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The rhythm of bioluminescence from modified firefly LUCIFERASE (LUC) genes coupled to the clock-controlled promoter was successfully used to map QTLs for circadian parameters.
source: More recently, the rhythm of bioluminescence from modified firefly LUCIFERASE (LUC) genes coupled to the clock-controlled promoter was successfully used to map QTLs for circadian parameters (Darrah et al., 2006; Boikoglou et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Darrah et al., 2006 and Boikoglou et al., 2011.

claim: A total of 71 RILs derived from the genetic cross of Bayreuth-0 and Shakdara (BxS) were modified to harbor the CCR2 promoter fused to luciferase (CCR2::LUC).
source: A total of 71 RILs derived from the genetic cross of Bayreuth-0 and Shakdara (BxS) were modified to harbor the CCR2 promoter, also termed GRP7 (Loudet et al., 2002), fused to luciferase (CCR2::LUC).
evidence: This describes the experimental materials used.

claim: Extensive variation in periodicity was observed in BxS RILs after photic and thermal entrainment.
source: These lines were synchronized to respective photic and thermal entrainment, and free-running periodicity was assessed under identical conditions of constant light and constant temperature. After applying both entrainment protocols, extensive variation in periodicity was observed (Figure 1A; Supplementary file 1, Supplementary file 2)
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1A and supplementary files.

claim: The two parental ecotypes (Bay-0 and Sha) displayed similar periodicity, irrespective of preceding entrainment.
source: however, the two parental ecotypes displayed similar periodicity, irrespective of preceding entrainment.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing the results.

claim: A significant shift for shortened free-running periodicity of CCR2 after thermal entrainment was observed for the parental lines and RILs compared to photic entrainment.
source: Compared to photic entrainment, a significant shift for shortened free-running periodicity of CCR2 after thermal entrainment was observed for the parental lines, as well as RILs (Figure 1A–C; Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1A-C and Table 1.

claim: The periodicity differences after photic vs thermal entrainment (Period LD–Period TMP) extended from minus 0.56 hr to plus 1.66 hr.
source: The periodicity differences after respective photic vs thermal entrainment (Period Light Dark (LD)–Period TMP [TMP]) extended from minus 0.56 hr to plus 1.66 hr (Figure 1B,C; Table 1)
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1B,C and Table 1.

claim: Parental lines displayed periodicity differences of plus 1.84 and plus 2.15 hr for Sha and Bay-0, respectively.
source: with parental lines displaying periodicity differences of plus 1.84 and plus 2.15 hr for Sha and Bay-0, respectively (Boikoglou et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to Boikoglou et al., 2011.

claim: The averaged periodicity differences of BxS lines were moderate (0.433, p<0.001).
source: The averaged periodicity differences of BxS lines were moderate (0.433, p<0.001) (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Table 1.

claim: CCR2 free-running periodicity followed a normal distribution regardless of the entrainment zeitgeber.
source: CCR2 free-running periodicity followed a normal distribution regardless of the entrainment zeitgeber, where lower and higher extreme periodicities were measured in thermal and photic entrainment, respectively (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1A.

claim: Statistically significant G by E interactions were found for CCR2 periodicity in BxS RILs.
source: The normally distributed phenotypes allowed us to test the fixed effects of entrainment (E) by the random effects of genotypes (G), and we found statistically significant G by E interactions (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Table 2.

claim: The factor with the most significant effect in period variation was environment, with genotypes having a lesser, albeit highly significant effect.
source: The factor with the most significant effect in period variation was environment, with genotypes having a lesser, albeit highly significant effect (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Table 2.

claim: When the genotypic effect was compared between RILs and transformants, a far greater variation in periodicity could be observed in RILs.
source: Moreover, when the genotypic effect was compared between RILs and transformants, a far greater variation in periodicity could be observed in RILs (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Table 2.

claim: Transformation-derived variation (position effects) was not a major component of detected variation.
source: Transformation-derived variation (position effects) was thus not a major component of detected variation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data in Table 2.

claim: Trait heritabilities for photic and thermal entrainment were 0.76 and 0.73, respectively.
source: Our efforts then focused on mapping the genetic components of differential periodicity of the two inputs. This resulted in the identification of three large-effect QTLs for photic entrainment on chromosomes 1, 2, and 4. Two co-localized QTLs were found on chromosomes 2 and 4 (Table 3). The QTL on Chromosome 2 (Chr2) displayed the largest phenotypic effect and we thus pursued its identification.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Table 3.

claim: Three large-effect QTLs for photic entrainment were identified on chromosomes 1, 2, and 4.
source: This resulted in the identification of three large-effect QTLs for photic entrainment on chromosomes 1, 2, and 4.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing QTL mapping results.

claim: Two co-localized QTLs were found on chromosomes 2 and 4.
source: Two co-localized QTLs were found on chromosomes 2 and 4 (Table 3).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Table 3.

claim: The QTL on Chromosome 2 (Chr2) displayed the largest phenotypic effect.
source: The QTL on Chromosome 2 (Chr2) displayed the largest phenotypic effect and we thus pursued its identification.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing QTL mapping results.

claim: HIF-Sha always displayed a shorter period compared to HIF-Bay-0, independent of the preceding LD or TMP entrainment condition.
source: An analysis of the free-running period of these lines revealed that HIF-Sha always displayed a shorter period as compared to HIF-Bay-0. This period-shortening effect was independent of the preceding LD or TMP entrainment condition (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2A.

claim: NIL-S displayed a 2-hr shorter period compared to Bay-0 under LL.
source: Consistent with the HIFs, NIL-S displayed a 2-hr shorter period, as compared to Bay-0, which was only observed under LL.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing NIL-S periodicity.

claim: In DD, no significant period difference was detected between NIL-S and Bay-0.
source: In DD, no significant period difference was detected (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2B.

claim: In DD, CCR2::LUC rhythmicity lost robustness in NIL-S, whereas CCR2::LUC in Bay-0 displayed rhythms for 7 days.
source: However, in DD, the free-running profile of CCR2::LUC in NIL-S was different from the Bay parental line, so that, in NIL-S, CCR2::LUC rhythmicity lost robustness, whereas CCR2::LUC in Bay-0 displayed rhythms for 7 days (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3A.

claim: Under both LL and in DD, the Sha parental line displayed a CCR2::LUC profile similar to that of Bay-0, and different from NIL-S.
source: Interestingly, under both LL and in DD, the Sha parental line displayed a CCR2::LUC profile similar to that of Bay-0, and different from NIL-S (Figures 2B and 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figures 2B and 3A.

claim: Fine mapping delineated the Chr2 QTL region to a 40-Kb interval with nine annotated genes.
source: We next employed a fine-mapping strategy to isolate the Chr2 QTL and delineated the region to a 40-Kb interval with nine annotated genes (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2C.

claim: ELF3 (AT2G25930) was the only gene in the 40-Kb region with a previously reported function in the Arabidopsis circadian clock.
source: ELF3 (AT2G25930) was the only gene in this region with a previously reported function in the Arabidopsis circadian clock.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing the fine-mapping results.

claim: ELF3-Sha has two nonsynonymous changes compared to ELF3-Bay: an encoded alanine-to-valine transition at position 362 (A362V), and in the C-terminal encoded glutamine stretch, Sha had 8 more than Bay.
source: Therefore, we compared the sequence of ELF3-Bay and ELF3-Sha and identified two nonsynonymous changes in ELF3-Sha: an encoded alanine-to-valine transition at position 362 (A362V), and in the C-terminal encoded glutamine stretch, Sha had 8 more than Bay (Figure 3C; and as reported [Tajima et al., 2007; Coluccio et al., 2011]).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3C, with citations to prior reports.

claim: HIF 89-S showed modestly advanced flowering time under short days compared to HIF 539-B.
source: While we observed no large differences in flowering time under long days, HIF 89-S showed modestly advanced flowering time under short days, compared to HIF 539-B (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4A.

claim: No substantial difference in the hypocotyl length of HIFs, NIL-S, and Bay-0 was observed under RR or BB.
source: Similar to the near lack of flowering-time phenotype under long days, we did not observe a substantial difference in the hypocotyl length of HIFs, NIL-S, and Bay-0 under RR or BB.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing hypocotyl measurements.

claim: Under short days, HIF 89-S displayed a marginally elongated hypocotyl length compared to HIF 539-B, but this response was four times less than that seen in the null elf3.
source: Under short days, however, HIF 89-S displayed a marginally elongated hypocotyl length, compared to HIF 539-B, but this response was four times less than that seen in the null elf3 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4B.

claim: A NIL that harbored ELF3-Sha in a Bay background did not display substantial physiological effects under normal growth conditions.
source: Overall, a NIL that harbored ELF3-Sha in a Bay background did not display substantial physiological effects under normal growth conditions, indicating that ELF3-Sha maintains developmental activity lost in null elf3 alleles.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the flowering time and hypocotyl data.

claim: T2 transgenic lines harboring ELF3-Sha-YFP displayed a consistent short period under LL compared to lines harboring ELF3-Bay-YFP for both LHY::LUC and CCR2::LUC.
source: The free-running period analysis of T2 transgenic lines harboring ELF3-Sha-YFP displayed a consistent short period under LL, compared to the lines harboring ELF3-Bay-YFP, for both LHY::LUC and CCR2::LUC (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3B.

claim: Based on complementation experiments, ELF3 was confirmed as quantitative trait gene (QTG) underlying the Chr2 periodicity QTL.
source: Based on these complementation experiments, we confirmed ELF3 as quantitative trait gene (QTG) underlying the Chr2 periodicity QTL.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the complementation experiments.

claim: Lines SpSc and SpBa2v that contained encoded valine displayed a shorter period compared to the SpBc and SpSv2a lines harboring encoded alanine, irrespective of the number of glutamines present.
source: We observed that lines SpSc and SpBa2v that contained encoded valine displayed a shorter period as compared to the SpBc and SpSv2a lines harboring encoded alanine, irrespective of the number of glutamines present (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5B.

claim: Both ELF3-Bay and ELF3-A362V displayed a robust rhythm of LHY::LUC expression under LL, albeit with lower amplitude observed in ELF3-A362V.
source: Both ELF3-Bay and ELF3-A362V displayed a robust rhythm of LHY::LUC expression under LL, albeit with lower amplitude observed in ELF3-A362V (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5C.

claim: In DD, ELF3-A362V failed to maintain robust rhythms after 4 days in darkness and displayed an acute dampening of LHY::LUC expression, whereas ELF3-Bay displayed robust rhythm of LHY::LUC even after 6 days in darkness.
source: However, in DD, the expression profile of LHY::LUC in ELF3-Bay and ELF3-A362V was distinctly different. ELF3-A362V failed to maintain robust rhythms after 4 days in darkness and displayed an acute dampening of LHY::LUC expression, whereas ELF3-Bay displayed robust rhythm of LHY::LUC, even after 6 days in darkness (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5D.

claim: The period analysis of LHY::LUC expression revealed no statistically significant period difference between ELF3-Bay and ELF3-A362V in DD, whereas under LL, ELF3-A362V displayed a shorter period compared to ELF3-Bay.
source: The period analysis of LHY::LUC expression in ELF3-Bay and ELF3-A362V revealed no statistically significant period difference in DD, whereas under LL, ELF3-A362V displayed a shorter period compared to ELF3-Bay (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5E.

claim: The encoded A362V polymorphism is the functionally encoded variant in Sha sufficient to explain the Chr2 periodicity QTL in the BxS population.
source: These results are consistent with those described above for both HIFs and NIL-S and support that the encoded A362V polymorphism is the functionally encoded variant in Sha sufficient to explain the Chr2 periodicity QTL in the BxS population (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the A362V experiments.

claim: Both ELF3-Bay and ELF3-A362V displayed robust LHY::LUC expression so long as they remained under light.
source: We observed that both ELF3-Bay and ELF3-A362V displayed robust LHY::LUC expression so long as they remained under light (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6A.

claim: When plants were transferred to darkness, LHY::LUC expression dampened more rapidly in ELF3-A362V.
source: However, when the plants were transferred to darkness, LHY::LUC expression dampened more rapidly in ELF3-A362V.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing the light-dark experiment.

claim: For ELF3-Bay, an acute reduction of LHY::LUC expression was seen such that proper rhythm was maintained throughout the dark period, while no detectable rhythmic expression of LHY::LUC was observed in ELF3-A362V.
source: For ELF3-Bay, an acute reduction of LHY::LUC expression was seen such that proper rhythm was maintained throughout the dark period, while no detectable rhythmic expression of LHY::LUC was observed in ELF3-A362V (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6A.

claim: Both ELF3-Bay and ELF3-A362V recovered robust rhythms of LHY::LUC after the 11-day treatment, including the 4-day period in darkness.
source: Both ELF3-Bay and ELF3-A362V recovered robust rhythms of LHY::LUC after the 11-day treatment, including the 4-day period in darkness (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6A.

claim: Light is necessary to sustain a robust oscillator in the context of ELF3-A362V.
source: These results suggested that light is necessary to sustain a robust oscillator in the context of ELF3-A362V.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the light-dark experiment results.

claim: Under LL, ELF3-A362V displayed a ∼1.5-hr short period compared to ELF3-Bay, with both lines showing high precision (R.A.E. <0.20).
source: Under LL, ELF3-A362V displayed a ∼1.5-hr short period compared to ELF3-Bay, with both lines showing high precision (R.A.E. <0.20; Figures 6B and 7A, ZT40-120).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figures 6B and 7A.

claim: In darkness, while both ELF3-Bay and ELF3-A362V had similar period estimates, ELF3-A362V did not maintain precision and displayed high R.A.E. (R.A.E. >0.75), compared to ELF3-Bay (R.A.E. <0.35).
source: However, in darkness, while both lines had similar period estimates, ELF3-A362V did not maintain precision and displayed high R.A.E. (R.A.E. >0.75), compared to ELF3-Bay (R.A.E. <0.35; Figures 6B and 7B, ZT160-240).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figures 6B and 7B.

claim: The loss of precision of LHY::LUC rhythm was recovered in ELF3-A362V when the plants were returned to the light at ZT250.
source: Interestingly, the loss of precision of LHY::LUC rhythm was recovered in ELF3-A362V when the plants were returned to the light at ZT250 (Figures 6B and 7C, ZT260-340).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figures 6B and 7C.

claim: LHY::LUC peaked at a similar time in both ELF3-Bay and ELF3-A362V, which in part was determined by the duration of the dark period.
source: We found that LHY::LUC peaked at a similar time in both ELF3-Bay and ELF3-A363V, which in part was determined by the duration of the dark period.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing the phase shift experiment.

claim: No significant phase difference between ELF3-Bay and ELF3-A362V was detected at any time point tested in the phase shift experiment.
source: This revealed the presence of a partially functional oscillator during the dark period in both these lines. Further, no significant phase difference between these lines was detected at any time point tested (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 8A.

claim: Once the plants were transferred back to the light, robust rhythms of LHY::LUC were restored in both ELF3-Bay and ELF3-A362V.
source: Interestingly, consistent with the above results (Figure 6A), once the plants were transferred back to the light, robust rhythms of LHY::LUC were restored (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 8B.

claim: In a phase–difference graph (Phase ELF3-Bay minus Phase ELF3-A362V), a consistent pattern of phase oscillations was detected, supporting the existence of a functional oscillator in both ELF3-Bay and ELF3-A362V that display differences in their respective resetting behavior.
source: Notably, in a phase–difference graph (Phase ELF3-Bay minus Phase ELF3-A362V), a consistent pattern of phase oscillations was detected, supporting the existence of a functional oscillator in both ELF3-Bay and ELF3-A362V that display differences in their respective resetting behavior (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6C.

claim: ELF3-Sha requires light input to maintain precision of the circadian clock.
source: Taken together, we concluded that ELF3-Sha requires light input to maintain precision of the circadian clock; however, darkness does not fully abolish the low-amplitude oscillation in ELF3-Sha plants and that entrainment processes appear altered.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the phase shift and precision experiments.

claim: Darkness does not fully abolish the low-amplitude oscillation in ELF3-Sha plants.
source: Taken together, we concluded that ELF3-Sha requires light input to maintain precision of the circadian clock; however, darkness does not fully abolish the low-amplitude oscillation in ELF3-Sha plants and that entrainment processes appear altered.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the phase shift and precision experiments.

claim: Entrainment processes appear altered in ELF3-Sha.
source: Taken together, we concluded that ELF3-Sha requires light input to maintain precision of the circadian clock; however, darkness does not fully abolish the low-amplitude oscillation in ELF3-Sha plants and that entrainment processes appear altered.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experiments.

claim: Under diverse intensities and qualities of light, NIL-S displayed a shorter period than Bay.
source: Under diverse intensities and qualities of light, we found that NIL-S displayed a shorter period than Bay.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing the fluence rate experiments.

claim: Both Bay and NIL-S followed Aschoff's rule, displaying shortening of periodicity with increase in fluence rate.
source: Moreover, both Bay and NIL-S followed Aschoff's rule, displaying shortening of periodicity with increase in fluence rate (Figure 9A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 9A-C.

claim: Wild-type plants with a functional clock entrained under 24-hr environmental cycles (T24) maintain the same rhythms when transferred to shorter cycles (T12).
source: Wild-type plants with a functional clock entrained under 24-hr environmental cycles (T24) maintain the same rhythms when transferred to shorter cycles (T12).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about frequency demultiplication.

claim: Mutants with a dysfunctional clock promptly follow the shorter cycles (T12) when transferred from T24 to T12.
source: Conversely, when transferred from T24 to T12, mutants with a dysfunctional clock promptly follow the shorter cycles (Nozue et al., 2007; Thines and Harmon, 2010; Kolmos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: In null elf3 mutants, LHY::LUC completely followed the T12 cycles, revealing a dysfunctional clock.
source: As previously reported for null elf3 (Kolmos et al., 2011), we detected a driven 24 hr rhythm, and, thereafter, LHY::LUC completely followed the T12 cycles in this mutant, revealing, in turn, a dysfunctional clock (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6D, with citation.

claim: Both Ws-2 and ELF3-Bay initially resisted the T12 cycles for 3 days, displaying driven T24 rhythms, but after 3 days showed robust adaptation to the T12 cycles.
source: As expected, both Ws-2 and ELF3-Bay initially resisted the T12 cycles for 3 days, displaying driven T24 rhythms. However, after 3 days, both Ws-2 and ELF3-Bay showed a robust adaptation to the T12 cycles, which were observed as strong LHY::LUC peaks matching the peaks expected for T12 cycles (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6D.

claim: ELF3-A362V did not show adaptation to T12 cycles, and strong LHY::LUC peaks completely matched the T24 cycles for all 5 days.
source: Interestingly, ELF3-A362V did not show this effect in T12 cycles, and strong LHY::LUC peaks completely matched the T24 cycles for all 5 days (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6D.

claim: ELF3-Sha failed to perceive persistent new environmental signals, revealing that the circadian oscillator in ELF3-Sha is defective in proper entrainment resetting.
source: Since both Ws-2 and ELF3-Bay responded to persistent T12 cycles, while ELF3-Sha did not, we concluded from these results that ELF3-Sha failed to perceive persistent new environmental signals, revealing that the circadian oscillator in ELF3-Sha is indeed defective in proper entrainment resetting.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the frequency demultiplication experiment.

claim: elf3 loss-of-function alleles display arrhythmia under continuous light and in darkness.
source: Under continuous light and in darkness, it has been reported that elf3 loss-of-function alleles display arrhythmia (Hicks et al., 1996; Thines and Harmon, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Expression profiling revealed that elf3 had reduced expression of the core oscillator genes CCA1 and LHY, but high levels of the evening genes TOC1 and GI.
source: Accordingly, expression profiling revealed that elf3 had reduced expression of the core oscillator genes CCA1 and LHY, but high levels of the evening genes TOC1 and GI (Fowler et al., 1999; Kikis et al., 2005; Dixon et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Under LL, ELF3-Sha was rhythmic for all clock genes studied and displayed an intermediate level of expression compared to wild type and loss-of-function elf3.
source: In contrast, under LL, ELF3-Sha was rhythmic for all genes studied, and it displayed an intermediate level of expression compared to wild type and loss-of-function elf3 (Figure 10A–F, left panels).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 10A-F.

claim: NIL-S displayed higher expression of TOC1 and GI compared to Bay-0, but lower expression than elf3-1 and elf3-4.
source: Specifically, NIL-S displayed higher expression of TOC1 and GI compared to Bay-0, but lower expression than elf3-1 and elf3-4.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing the clock gene expression results.

claim: Expression of CCA1 and LHY was lower in NIL-S compared to Bay-0, but higher than elf3-4.
source: In contrast, expression of CCA1 and LHY was lower in NIL-S, compared to Bay-0, but higher than elf3-4.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing the clock gene expression results.

claim: A higher transcript abundance of PRR7 and PRR9 was observed in NIL-S.
source: Consistent with the previous finding that CCA1 and LHY regulate PRR7 and PRR9 (Farre et al., 2005; Nakamichi et al., 2010), a higher transcript abundance of PRR7 and PRR9 was observed in NIL-S (Figures 10E,F and 11C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figures 10E,F and 11C,D, with citations.

claim: The evening complex (ELF3, ELF4, and LUX) directly binds to the PRR9 promoter to repress transcription.
source: These data, along with recent findings showing the evening complex (ELF3, ELF4, and LUX) directly binds to the PRR9 promoter to repress transcription, support the repressive action of ELF3 in the core oscillator (Helfer et al., 2011; Nusinow et al., 2011; Chow et al., 2012; Herrero et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with citations to recent findings.

claim: The double loss-of-function mutant cca1-11 lhy-21 is rhythmic.
source: Considering the double loss-of-function mutant cca1-11 lhy-21 is rhythmic, an additional repressive role of ELF3 by targeted degradation of GI is conceptually plausible (Ding et al., 2007; Yu et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with citations.

claim: ELF3 is both a cytosolic and nuclear localized protein.
source: ELF3 is both a cytosolic and nuclear localized protein.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: ELF3 has several binding partners including phyB, COP1, ELF4, and GI.
source: It appears to be multifunctional in that it has several binding partners. These include phyB, COP1, ELF4, and GI (Yu et al., 2008; Nusinow et al., 2011; Herrero et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with citations.

claim: Both phyB and COP1 interact with the N-terminal domain of ELF3.
source: Both phyB and COP1 interact with the N-terminal domain (Liu et al., 2001; Yu et al., 2008; Kolmos et al., 2011)
evidence: This is stated with citations.

claim: ELF4 and GI interact with the middle domain of ELF3.
source: whereas ELF4 and GI interact with the middle domain (Yu et al., 2008; Herrero et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with citations.

claim: All ELF3 binding proteins co-localize in the nucleus where they form distinct nuclear bodies.
source: Further, all these proteins co-localize in the nucleus where they form distinct nuclear bodies (Mas et al., 2000; Yu et al., 2008; Chen et al., 2010; Herrero et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with citations.

claim: The rhythmic accumulation of both ELF3 and GI depends upon the activity of COP1 that mediates ubiquitination and targeted degradation of these proteins in dark conditions.
source: The rhythmic accumulation of both ELF3 and GI depends upon the activity of COP1 that mediates ubiquitination and targeted degradation of these proteins in dark conditions (Yu et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with citation.

claim: ELF3 is essential for COP1-mediated GI degradation; in the absence of ELF3, COP1 cannot interact with GI.
source: It is noteworthy here that ELF3 is essential for this process. In the absence of ELF3, COP1 cannot interact with GI and thus cannot initiate its decay.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: GI is not required for COP1-mediated ELF3 degradation.
source: However, GI is not required for COP1-mediated ELF3 degradation (Yu et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with citation.

claim: The mean level of ELF3-Sha transcript was slightly higher relative to ELF3-Bay.
source: We found that the mean level of ELF3-Sha transcript was slightly higher relative to ELF3-Bay.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing transcript measurements.

claim: Higher ELF3-Sha protein accumulation was detected in comparison to ELF3-Bay, as measured by the ELF3-YFP signals.
source: Correspondingly, higher ELF3-Sha protein accumulation was detected in comparison to ELF3-Bay, as measured by the ELF3-YFP signals (Figure 12A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 12A-D.

claim: The formation of distinct nuclear bodies was markedly attenuated in ELF3-Sha, whereas these nuclear bodies were clearly observable in ELF3-Bay.
source: Specifically, the formation of distinct nuclear bodies, a characteristic of ELF3 (Herrero et al., 2012), was markedly attenuated in ELF3-Sha, whereas these nuclear bodies were clearly observable in ELF3-Bay (Figure 12A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 12A,B, with citation.

claim: The preferential nuclear localization of ELF3 was compromised in ELF3-Sha, which displayed a markedly elevated amount of cytoplasmic content compared to ELF3-Bay.
source: Additionally, the preferential nuclear localization of ELF3 was compromised in ELF3-Sha, which displayed a markedly elevated amount of cytoplasmic content, compared to ELF3-Bay (Figure 12A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 12A-D.

claim: The nuclear–cytoplasmic ratio of ELF3-Sha was four times less than that of ELF3-Bay.
source: Quantification of YFP revealed that the nuclear–cytoplasmic ratio of ELF3-Sha was four times less than that of ELF3-Bay (Figure 12E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 12E.

claim: Localization defects of ELF3-Sha underlie its oscillator defects.
source: As such, we proposed that these localization defects of ELF3-Sha underlie its oscillator defects.
evidence: This is stated as a proposal based on the localization data.

claim: Under LD, only a minor increase in ELF3-Sha transcript and protein levels was found compared to ELF3-Bay.
source: Under LD, we found only a minor increase in ELF3-Sha transcript and protein levels compared to ELF3-Bay (Figure 13A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 13A,B.

claim: Under LL, the ELF3-Sha transcript was significantly higher at all time-points compared to ELF3-Bay, which also resulted in elevated levels of ELF3-Sha protein.
source: However, under LL, the ELF3-Sha transcript was significantly higher at all time-points compared to ELF3-Bay, which also resulted in elevated levels of ELF3-Sha protein (Figure 13C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 13C,D.

claim: Compared to LD where ELF3 accumulation decreased during the evening hours, elevated protein levels of both ELF3-Bay and ELF3-Sha were found during subjective night (ZT16 and ZT20) under LL.
source: Furthermore, compared to LD where ELF3 accumulation decreased during the evening hours, we found elevated protein levels of both ELF3-Bay and ELF3-Sha during subjective night (ZT16 and ZT20).
evidence: This is stated in the text describing the LL protein accumulation.

claim: In DD, ELF3-Sha transcript levels were higher compared to ELF3-Bay.
source: In DD, similar to LL, ELF3-Sha transcript levels were higher compared to ELF3-Bay.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing the DD results.

claim: In DD, no significant difference in ELF3-Bay and ELF3-Sha protein levels was detected during subjective day, whereas during subjective night (ZT16 and ZT 20), ELF3-Sha accumulation was considerably lower than ELF3-Bay.
source: However, we did not detect any significant difference in ELF3-Bay and ELF3-Sha protein levels during subjective day, whereas during subjective night (ZT16 and ZT 20), we found that ELF3-Sha accumulation was considerably lower than ELF3-Bay (Figure 13E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 13E,F.

claim: ELF3-Sha protein dissipates in darkness comparatively more rapidly than ELF3-Bay.
source: Taken together, a higher accumulation of ELF3-Sha under LL and overall lower levels in DD, despite higher transcript abundance, led us to conclude that ELF3-Sha protein dissipates in darkness comparatively more rapidly than ELF3-Bay.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the protein accumulation data.

claim: The sequence comparison of 251 accessions revealed the presence of 59 polymorphic sites segregating at the ELF3 locus, including encoded A362V.
source: The sequence comparison revealed the presence of 59 polymorphic sites segregating at the ELF3 locus, including encoded A362V.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing the population genetics analysis.

claim: Out of 59 polymorphic sites at the ELF3 locus, 16 were synonymous and 43 were nonsynonymous.
source: Out of these 59 polymorphic sites, 16 were synonymous and 43 were nonsynonymous.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing the population genetics analysis.

claim: The A362V polymorphism was detected in 15 accessions, and in a phylogenetic analysis, all of these grouped together in a single clade, suggesting a common origin.
source: The A362V was detected in 15 accessions, and in a phylogenetic analysis, all of these grouped together in a single clade, suggesting a common origin (Figure 14A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 14A.

claim: All accessions with the A362V polymorphism were distributed in Central Asia between 37°N and 54°N, with two exceptions at Nemrut and Rubenzhoe collected from Turkey and the Ukraine, respectively.
source: Therefore, we looked at the geographical distribution of these accessions and found that they all were distributed in Central Asia between 37°N and 54°N, with two exceptions at Nemrut and Rubenzhoe collected from Turkey and the Ukraine, respectively (Figure 14B; Table 4).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 14B and Table 4.

claim: Similar to Sha that naturally grows at high altitudes, most accessions with A362V were also high-altitude accessions collected in the mountains.
source: Interestingly, similar to Sha that naturally grows at high altitudes (e.g., Pamir Mountains, Tajikistan), most of these accessions were also high-altitude accessions collected in the mountains (Table 4).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Table 4.

claim: ELF3-Sha originated from Central Asia and this allele might have been maintained during species migration preferentially by altitude-associated individuals.
source: These results suggest that ELF3-Sha originated from Central Asia and that this allele might have been maintained during species migration preferentially by altitude-associated individuals.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the geographical distribution data.

claim: ELF3 has been established as a required component for the generation of circadian rhythms and the perception of light and temperature inputs.
source: ELF3 has been established as a required component for the generation of circadian rhythms and the perception of light and temperature inputs (Covington et al., 2001; Thines and Harmon, 2010; Kolmos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with citations in the discussion.

claim: Most elf3 alleles used in previous studies were identified in mutagenesis screens and displayed arrhythmicity under free-running conditions of LL and DD.
source: However, most of the elf3 alleles used in these studies were identified in mutagenesis screens, and many of them displayed arrhythmicity under free-running conditions of LL and DD.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: ELF3-Sha displayed a light-dependent short-period phenotype.
source: Here, we report the cloning and characterization of ELF3-Sha as a natural allele of ELF3, which displayed a light-dependent short-period phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: Unlike elf3 loss-of-function mutants, ELF3-Sha displayed robust circadian rhythms under continuous light.
source: Unlike elf3 loss-of-function mutants, this allelic state displayed robust circadian rhythms under continuous light.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: In prolonged darkness, the expression profile of many clock genes was dramatically damped in ELF3-Sha.
source: However, in prolonged darkness, the expression profile of many clock genes was dramatically damped (Figure 10).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by Figure 10.

claim: Proper cellular distribution of ELF3 is required to perform normal repressive function in the circadian clock.
source: The association between the clock phenotypes of ELF3-Sha and their cellular basis led us to conclude that proper cellular distribution of ELF3 is required to perform normal repressive function in the circadian clock (Figures 12 and 13) which in turn, depends on its cyclic accumulation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the discussion and supported by Figures 12 and 13.

claim: ELF3's normal repressive function depends on its cyclic accumulation.
source: The association between the clock phenotypes of ELF3-Sha and their cellular basis led us to conclude that proper cellular distribution of ELF3 is required to perform normal repressive function in the circadian clock (Figures 12 and 13) which in turn, depends on its cyclic accumulation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the discussion and supported by Figures 12 and 13.

claim: The identification and validation of quantitative trait loci (QTLs) by genetic mapping is a well-established procedure.
source: The identification and validation of quantitative trait loci (QTLs) by genetic mapping is a well-established procedure.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion.

claim: To understand the molecular basis of a locus by characterizing QTL to a quantitative trait nucleotide (QTN) level is still an arduous task.
source: However, to understand the molecular basis of a locus by characterizing QTL to a quantitative trait nucleotide (QTN) level is still an arduous task (Koornneef et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated with citation in the discussion.

claim: The periodicity results for ELF3-Sha were consistent with previous studies where the ELF3 in Sha was found to modulate the shade-avoidance response, including the action of shade on the oscillator.
source: Our periodicity results were consistent with previous studies where the ELF3 in Sha was found to modulate the shade-avoidance response, including the action of shade on the oscillator (Jimenez-Gomez et al., 2010; Coluccio et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with citations in the discussion.

claim: The light-dependent acceleration of circadian oscillations of ELF3-Sha could be associated with reduced ELF3 functionality.
source: The light-dependent acceleration of circadian oscillations of ELF3-Sha could be associated with reduced ELF3 functionality (McWatters et al., 2000; Covington et al., 2001; Kolmos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with citations in the discussion.

claim: The intermediate expression profile of several clock genes in ELF3-Sha confirmed that it is a hypomorphic allele.
source: The intermediate expression profile of several clock genes in ELF3-Sha, when compared to wild-type and null mutants, confirmed that it is a hypomorphic allele (Figures 10 and 11).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by Figures 10 and 11.

claim: ELF3-Sha is distinctly different from elf3 null mutants, which displayed complete arrhythmia under LL.
source: This characteristic of ELF3-Sha is distinctly different from elf3 null mutants, which displayed complete arrhythmia under LL (Covington et al., 2001; Hicks et al., 2001; Thines and Harmon, 2010; Kolmos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with citations in the discussion.

claim: ELF3 is required for robust oscillation in darkness.
source: Thus, our results conclusively demonstrate that ELF3 is required for robust oscillation in darkness and further support the idea that ELF3 is an integral part of the oscillator (Thines and Harmon, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the discussion with citation.

claim: The function of ELF3 is collectively defined by both the light–dark boundary and by circadian clock regulation.
source: Consequently, we further propose that the function of ELF3 is collectively defined by both the light–dark boundary and by circadian clock regulation.
evidence: This is stated as a proposal in the discussion.

claim: ELF3 plays a pivotal role in defining entrainment properties of the circadian clock, which depend on cyclic accumulation of ELF3 protein, but not on its absolute levels or transcript abundance.
source: Based on these results and our observation that ELF3-Sha is defective in proper clock resetting (Figure 6D), we propose that ELF3 plays a pivotal role in defining entrainment properties of the circadian clock, which, in turn, depend on cyclic accumulation of ELF3 protein, but not on its absolute levels or, indirectly, its transcript abundance.
evidence: This is stated as a proposal in the discussion and supported by Figure 6D.

claim: ELF3 protein rhythmically oscillates and drives a long period in plants that constitutively overexpress ELF3.
source: This idea could be further supported by the observation that ELF3 protein rhythmically oscillates and drives a long period in plants that constitutively overexpress ELF3 (Covington et al., 2001; Dixon et al., 2011; Herrero et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with citations in the discussion.

claim: It can be provisionally excluded that ELF3 is involved in parametric entrainment because no differential effect of fluence rate on ELF3-Sha periodicity compared to ELF3-Bay was detected.
source: Discounting the important role that ELF3 plays in clock entrainment, it can be provisionally excluded that ELF3 is involved in parametric entrainment because we could not detect any differential effect of fluence rate on ELF3-Sha periodicity compared to ELF3-Bay (Figure 9A–C).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the discussion and supported by Figure 9A-C.

claim: In the context of the Ws-2 and Bay-0 genomes, ELF3-Sha is a hypomorphic allele defective in proper localization of encoded ELF3 protein.
source: Notably, in the context of the Ws-2 and Bay-0 genomes, we could show that ELF3-Sha is a hypomorphic allele defective in proper localization of encoded ELF3 protein.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the discussion.

claim: The localization defect of ELF3-Sha resulted in two distinct phenotypes: one displaying a light-dependent short period and the other exhibiting loss of rhythm robustness in darkness.
source: This defect resulted in two distinct phenotypes: one displaying a light-dependent short period and the other exhibiting loss of rhythm robustness in darkness.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: The Sha parental line did not display obvious circadian defects like those seen in NIL-S.
source: It is notable that Sha parental line did not itself display such obvious circadian defects (Figures 2B and 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by Figures 2B and 3A.

claim: The transcript profile of clock genes in Sha followed the same pattern as observed in Bay-0, and such pattern was distinct from that seen in NIL-S.
source: Related to this, the transcript profile of clock genes in Sha followed the same pattern as observed in Bay-0, and such pattern was distinct from that seen in NIL-S (Figure 11).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by Figure 11.

claim: Other segregating QTLs within Sha wild type may genetically interact with ELF3-Sha.
source: Moreover, ELF3-Sha did not affect hypocotyl length in NIL-S and Sha in the same way. Under all light qualities tested, the hypocotyl length of NIL-S was similar to that of Bay-0, but was significantly longer when compared to Sha (Figure 4B), leading to the possibility that other segregating QTLs within Sha wild type genetically interact with ELF3-Sha.
evidence: This is stated as a possibility in the discussion and supported by Figure 4B.

claim: Similar background-dependent effects of natural alleles have been reported in Arabidopsis for seed longevity, axillary bud formation, and flowering time.
source: Such similar background-dependent effects of natural alleles have been reported in Arabidopsis for seed longevity, axillary bud formation, and flowering time (Sugliani et al., 2009; Huang et al., 2012; Undurraga et al., 2012; Méndez-Vigo et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citations in the discussion.

claim: The ELF3-Sha allele is present in a group of genetically related accessions that are predominately distributed in a geographical area of Central Asia.
source: Our efforts to track the history of the ELF3-Sha revealed that this allele is present in a group of genetically related accessions that are predominately distributed in a geographical area of Central Asia (Figure 14A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by Figure 14A,B.

claim: The confined location of ELF3-Sha leads to the possibility that this allele provides local adaptive advantage to these accessions under their respective environmental conditions, and thus, has been positively selected during species migration.
source: This confined location of ELF3-Sha leads to the possibility that this allele provides local adaptive advantage to these accessions under their respective environmental conditions, and thus, has been positively selected during species migration.
evidence: This is stated as a possibility in the discussion.
